label: input q or y, or the <DEL> step
explanation: Low-precision, distributed unit. The main parts: (1) the <DEL> step (19% of DEL steps fire, 35% of mass; strongest when the sequence is long and the first token to recall is one of i/2/h/o/m/k, and it holds the top activations ~0.4); (2) input token q or y, which fires every time at t=0 (precision 1.0, 19% of mass) and less reliably later. Together these cover 76% of mass but only 23% precision. The rest is scattered copy-phase activity, mildly favoring out_tok in {i,2,h,o,m,k,n}. Rarely fires mid-original-phase (t=2..7) except on q/y. Gating DEL/q/y by the output token raises F1 only to 0.43.
